component.name: DriveSync
component.summary: Two-way Google Drive sync for Linux desktops

description.p: DriveSync keeps local folders and Google Drive in sync, with upload-only and download-only modes, conflict policies and an optional system tray icon.

A local web dashboard and a native desktop UI cover setup, account authorization and live activity; a background worker syncs on a schedule or on demand. Everything runs on your machine: tokens are stored locally and talk to Google directly with your own OAuth client.

ul.li: Bidirectional, upload-only and download-only sync per folder
Selective sync: choose which subfolders a pair mirrors
On-demand downloads: browse all of Drive, fetch files or whole folders when you need them — no mount required
Google Docs/Sheets/Slides/Drawings exported to open formats
Per-file activity log, filterable by action, level and time
Background worker with systemd user unit and tray integration

description.p: Security and workflow release. The dashboard API now requires a random per-server token, sign-in runs as a cancellable background job, removing an account can revoke its Google grant, and pair removals can be undone. Read-only Drive mode and optional OS keyring token storage are available in both the web and desktop settings.

The pairs list is now a card layout with live progress and per-pair actions, browser confirmations were replaced by an accessible dialog, and the desktop app watches local folders for instant sync. The systemd user unit is sandboxed, releases are built from a pinned dependency lockfile and now carry signed build provenance.

The published RPM now starts on hosts whose Python is older than the CI build image's: the app lives in a version-independent vendor directory instead of a versioned site-packages path. The AppImage payload layout was fixed (it could not find its own package), it can open the native GTK window when the desktop provides PyGObject/GTK 3, and its menu entry now launches that window instead of the browser dashboard.

Shared Drives are now first-class folder roots in the dashboard, the desktop app and the sync-pair picker. Settings can be exported and imported between machines without ever carrying OAuth tokens or the client secret, and a new 'drivesync audit' command checks credential and file permissions (with --fix). The release pipeline now publishes deb, rpm, AppImage and Flatpak artifacts with checksums. An optional read-only FUSE mount ('drivesync mount') and a Dolphin/KDE context menu round out the desktop integration.

Drive-tab downloads now show live progress: a spinner and a per-file line in the tab, with the result summary kept on screen afterwards. Starting a second download while one is running no longer silently does nothing — downloads run concurrently. Selected rows are now visibly highlighted on every system theme, and a Select all button was added for bulk downloads. The RPM spec builds again (stale Version tag and a malformed changelog date fixed; build-rpm.sh injects the real version).

On-demand downloads: a new Drive tab lists your whole Drive and downloads any file or folder to a destination you pick — like a virtual drive without the mount. Selective sync per pair: choose which subfolders mirror; the rest stays on Drive and on disk. Also fixed the desktop app always opening on the Setup tab on newer GTK, and launch crashes are now logged and shown instead of failing silently.

Instant local-change sync via inotify (watchdog), desktop notifications for conflicts and errors while the window is hidden, a --full rehash mode for same-mtime saves, a bandwidth cap and a daily sync window.

Friendlier command line: bare drivesync prints next steps, the config and pairs commands validate input with helpful errors, serve explains a busy dashboard port and can open the dashboard with --open, and the activity log now auto-prunes.

Fixed a crash when launching the desktop UI (activity list column type mismatch). Added software-center metadata so Discover and GNOME Software show developer info, release notes and the DriveSync icon.
Activity tab: newest-first list that keeps its place across refreshes, filters (action, level, time frame), sort toggle and a clear-log button.
